findings.evidence: Caption and white arrows identify capillary dropout on fluorescein angiography.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Fundus photograph from the right eye of a 3-year-old with bilateral Coats disease, showing the caption-specified exudates, exudative retinal detachment, and macular retinal fold. [raw subtype: stage 3A1] B: Fundus photograph from the left eye of the patient shows the caption-specified extrafoveal retinal exudation in stage 2A Coats disease. [raw subtype: stage 2A] C: Right-eye fluorescein angiogram demonstrates retinal capillary nonperfusion, a specific manifestation of Coats disease. D: Left-eye fluorescein angiogram shows capillary dropout, peripheral avascular retina, and adjacent retinal telangiectasia in Coats disease. E: SD-OCT section from the patient shows the caption-specified retinal thickening, hyperreflectivity, preretinal fibrosis, and retinal fold. These findings are not represented individually in the supplied controlled vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Piquin et al. Coats disease in female population: A comparison of clinical presentation and outcomes.. Frontiers in medicine 2022. doi:10.3389/fmed.2022.879110. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Bilateral Coats' disease in a 3-year-old girl. Right eye (A) is stage 3A1: fundus photograph shows an extrafoveal retinal detachment (red star) with exudates (black star) and a retinal fold at the level of the macula (blue arrow). Left eye (B) is stage 2A with extrafoveal exudation (black star). Fluorescein angiography shows capillary dropout (white arrows) in both eyes (C) right eye, (D) left eye) and a peripheral avascular retina (white star) lined with telangiectasia (red arrow) in the left eye. (E) SD-OCT section showing a thickening and hyperreflectivity of all retinal layers with preretinal fibrosis on top of the retinal fold.
